text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- As the constitutional debate rages, veteran politician John Keen suggests parliament should extend its life by one year to give it time to effect constitutional reforms before the next election.
- The Kenya Petroleum Refineries Ltd starts a 100-million-shilling project to accomodate larger liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) imports.
- The Uasin Gishu (Rift Valley Province) district commissioner Eliud Parkansul convenes a reconciliation meeting of ethnic Kikuyus and Kalenjins living in the Burnt Forest Area.

- Seven of the people condemned by doctors to permanent blindness after drinking laced chang'aa (locally brewed methyl alcohol) in Murang'a (central province) on the weekend of September 14-15 have regained eyesight.
- Tragedy strikes at Ndaragwa village in Nyandarua district (of Rift Valley province) as a mother of five drowns her four children before committing suicide.
- Six opposition FORD-Kenya parliament members revisit the 1990 death of former Foreign Affairs Minister Robert Ouko with a call to re-open the inquiry.
- Rival Somali faction leaders are said to be engrossed deeply in talks in Nairobi, but the venue of the exploratory peace talks remains a mystery.

- Kenya and Tanzania play significant roles in a decision by regional leaders in Arusha (Tanzania) to pursue a hardline against the military regime in Burundi by threatening further sanctions against coup leader Pierre Buyoya if he does not open unconditional talks with Hutu rebels within a month.

- Expressing satisfaction with Tanzania's economic reforms, World Bank representative in Dar es Salaam Ronald Brigish says the country will receive a soft loan of $100 million in balance of payments support next year.
